 Darius Acuff Jr. led the Kings with 34 points (13-of-26 FGs), six rebounds, 14 assists, one steal, three three-pointers and six turnovers in a 132-120 loss to the Pelicans on Thursday.
 The trend of Acuff’s field goal percentage improving every game continued in this one, which resulted in the best game of his young career. Acuff became just the fourth teenager in NBA history to have at least 30 points and 10 assists in a game, and while it didn’t lead to a win, it was an impressive performance. He cooled off in the second half after entering the break with 21 points, but it still led to a fantastic outing for the rookie in just his fifth game. It may not be this gaudy or efficient every night, but Acuff should continue to have plenty of usage all season.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Source:  Cameron Salerno

 Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 19 points (8-of-20 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 While the field-goal percentage remains relatively low, Acuff shot 40 percent from the field in Tuesday’s defeat. His percentage has increased in each of Sacramento’s first four games, and the rookie point guard has recorded 19 assists and 11 turnovers. Acuff still has plenty of work to do on efficiency, but he is making strides, which is good news for the Kings and fantasy managers.

 Guard

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Sunday’s loss to the Grizzlies with 22 points (9-of-23 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers. 
 After totaling seven assists in his first two games, Acuff matched that number on Sunday. The field-goal percentage wasn’t the best, but the points and assists were encouraging. Tuesday’s matchup with the Spurs will be challenging, given how good their young guards are offensively. It will be fun to see how Acuff takes on that test in the first of three games the Kings will play in Week 2.

 Darius Acuff puts up 33 points (10-of-26 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, and two threes in 128-120 loss to the Blazers. 
 The first thing you will see with Acuff is the points and get very excited. Then as you look at the rest of the stats, its pretty empty. He did get to the line 12 times and hit 11 which really should help your FT% category. While he did score a lot, especially in the second half when he got rolling, he will need to be better on the peripheral stats if he’s going to be a good category league player. He will have many more performances like this one later in the season.

 Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 12 points (5-of-24 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and three steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers. 
 Most fantasy managers and basketball fans expect rookie point guards to be inefficient. However, Acuff’s performance against the Clippers was rough. He missed all seven three-point attempts, shot 5-of-24 from the field, and finished with more turnovers (four) than assists (three). Acuff’s upside is undeniable, but he’ll have games like Wednesday.

 Darius Acuff Jr. had 13 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), one rebound, two assists, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s exhibition against the Spurs. 
 Acuff was -26 in 19 minutes, but all of the Kings’ starters were at least -21 as they lost to the Spurs by 29. He’s had an inconsistent preseason, which continued with 13 points on 12 attempts Friday. Acuff is going to get a ton of usage right away and has more than enough upside to justify his ADP, which is just outside the top-100.

 Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists and four three-pointers in Saturday’s exhibition against the Warriors. 
 After struggling in Thursday’s exhibition against the Lakers, Acuff was considerably better on Saturday. The lottery pick shot over 50 percent from the field and recorded a game-high eight assists. Even though it was just a preseason game, Acuff’s performance was encouraging, whether you’re a Kings fan or a fantasy manager considering drafting him in the later rounds of 12-team drafts.

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Thursday’s exhibition against the Lakers with 12 points (4-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one assist, two steals, one block and two three-pointers. 
 Outside of a solid finish to the first half, Acuff struggled mightily on Thursday. The rookie point guard missed his first nine field-goal attempts, and he finished with more turnovers (three) than assists (one). Reading too much into two preseason appearances would be foolish, but those who roster Acuff will need to exercise patience.

 Darius Acuff Jr. recorded 19 points (8-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 As expected, Acuff started at point guard in the Kings’ preseason opener. The lottery pick out of Arkansas led the team in shot attempts, which was unsurprising since he logged 27 minutes and no other starter played more than 15. Acuff shot reasonably well from the field overall, but he went 1-of-4 from beyond the arc and finished with more turnovers (five) than assists (four). Efficiency can be an issue for rookie point guards, but it seems clear Acuff will be given every opportunity to work through those struggles.

 NBA Insider Jake Fischer reports the Kings are considering re-signing Russell Westbrook and adding Victor Oladipo. 
 The report indicates the Kings are interested in adding a veteran mentor for Darius Acuff Jr., who they just selected with the 7th overall pick. Westbrook and Oladipo have experienced a lot during their NBA careers, so either would be a good locker room presence for Acuff to have around. However, with Acuff as the priority, neither would likely play enough to make much of an impact in fantasy basketball.

 Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 26 points (9-of-18 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Nets. 
 Acuff had a good afternoon in Las Vegas, but he did not have much help in a game the Kings lost by 32 points. The seventh overall pick in last month’s draft, Acuff shot the ball well against the Nets but finished with as many turnovers as assists (five). Given who he has shared the court with in Las Vegas, Acuff is likely to benefit from the Kings’ veterans being on the floor when the regular season kicks off. Efficiency can be an issue for rookie point guards, but the opportunity makes Acuff one of the top fantasy rookies in this class.

 Turner had his hands full with Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, who combined for 52 points and 16 rebounds.  Evan Mobley finished Saturday’s win over the Bucks with 27 points (11-of-16 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
 Cleveland removed most of the drama from Saturday’s game with a 48-point second quarter, led by Mobley. Shooting 5-of-5 from the field, he scored 13 points in the quarter, and frontcourt sidekick Jarrett Allen added nine. Mobley played just one minute in the fourth quarter, or his stat line could have been more robust.  Nickeil Alexander-Walker accounted for 12 points (3-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 Alexander-Walker had a rough night in New Orleans, missing all six of his three-point attempts. As a result, his streak of five straight games with at least two three-pointers to begin the season ended. Add in the lackluster assist and steal production, and this was a tough night for fantasy managers rostering Alexander-Walker. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday against the Pacers.

 Jalen Johnson (ankle) recorded 13 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 Johnson played the entire third quarter, but that would be the last we’d see of him on the court Saturday night. The Hawks forward sprained his left ankle, and while Johnson was questionable to return, he didn’t, as the game got out of hand. Atlanta’s four-game Week 3 begins on Monday against the Pacers and includes a back-to-back. If Johnson misses time, Aaron Wiggins (10/2/1/1/1 with two three-pointers) could become more important.

 Playing in New Orleans for the first time since he was traded to Washington in the summer of 2025, McCollum had a relatively quiet Saturday night.  While Williamson’s defensive effort has been questioned at times, he’s provided consistent value in steals this season.
